title: Skybase publishes prospective distribution partners with a Planning status before any relationship exists
content:
The In Progress Invocations Directory at A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.1.4 holds four prospective Instances — MetaMask (.4.1), InstaDapp (.4.2), Gnosis Protocol (.4.3) and Piku.co (.4.4) — each recorded with an explicit "Invocation Status: `Planning`" and a pointer to a configuration document that has already been allocated an address in the tree.

This is a governance framework doing something companies normally avoid: disclosing named counterparties at the planning stage, before terms are agreed and before either side is committed.

It follows from the Atlas's structure rather than from a disclosure policy. Because an Invocation is a document subtree that has to live somewhere, and the only destinations are the In Progress directory, the Active directory, or the archive, there is no unlisted staging area where an early-stage deal could sit. Transparency here is a consequence of state being expressed as location.

The consequences cut both ways. Prospective partners are informed that they are being courted, and observers can see the pipeline's health. But a deal that does not close does not merely vanish — it becomes an archived Failed Invocation under the Hub Data Repository, so unsuccessful business development leaves a permanent public trace. That raises the cost of speculative outreach and pushes an Agent to invoke only where it expects to complete.
description: MetaMask, InstaDapp, Gnosis Protocol and Piku.co sit in the In Progress Invocations directory with pre-allocated configuration documents, putting the business-development pipeline on the public
